modules.title: Your deck
modules.aiNote: AI may make or edit images, suggest layouts, and tighten sentences you wrote. It may not generate the deck or write your process decisions for you.

blocks.content:
**Nine slides. Slides 2 through 6 are one per station, in this order.**

```
SLIDE 1    Title. Your name, and a photo of your finished trophy.
SLIDE 2    BASE        H2D Laser
SLIDE 3    COLUMN      Manual Mill
SLIDE 4    PLATFORM    Axiom CNC Router
SLIDE 5    SHAFT       Manual Lathe
SLIDE 6    TOPPER      xTool MetalFab
SLIDE 7    Your measurements. Nominal, measured, difference.
SLIDE 8    What the numbers showed.
SLIDE 9    Rank the five processes. What you would do differently.
```

**On each station slide (2 through 6), three things:**

1. A photo of **your actual part**, not a render and not the model.
2. The one process decision that mattered most at that station.
3. What that station's part taught you about what the machine can and cannot hold.

**The rules on how it looks**

- **4:3 aspect ratio.** Set this before you start. Changing it later breaks your layouts.
- **25 words maximum on any slide.** Count them. This is the rule that makes the deck watchable.
- **Every slide has an image**, except the title slide if you want it clean.
- Slides carry what you point at. They do not carry what you say.

**The rules on what you build it in**

Your deck must open in **Google Slides, PowerPoint, or Canva**, and you must be able to export it to PDF.

If it only opens in its own web player, it does not count and you will present without slides.

You may use AI for images, for layout ideas, and to tighten your own writing. You may not have AI generate the deck for you. You will be asked about your own slides.

levels.label: Proficient

levels.label: Developing

levels.label: Complete

modules.intro: You walk the class through your trophy and what you found making it. Slides are on the screen. Your five parts are on the bench in front of you.
modules.title: Present your portfolio

blocks.content:
**Seven minutes each. Five minutes presenting, two minutes of questions.**

The timer is real. At five minutes you stop, wherever you are.

**How the days work**

- **Block 3:** presentations run across two class days. Half the class each day. The order is posted before the first day.
- **Blocks 2 and 4:** every presentation happens in one class day.

Your deck is due before the **first** presentation day either way. If you present on the second day, your deck was still due on the first.

**What you have to cover in five minutes**

- The most significant process decision you made at each of the five stations.
- What your measurements showed about which processes held the dimensions and which did not.
- **Why** that happened. Not that the printer hole was small, but what about that process made it small.

**The two minutes of questions**

Questions come from the instructor and from the class. They are about what you did and what you measured, not about whether your choices were right. Everyone made the same five parts.

Reading your slides out loud is not an answer. If you do not know, say so and say what you would measure to find out.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Names a specific process decision at all five stations, each one a choice that could have gone another way.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Names a specific decision at four stations, or covers all five but one is a description rather than a decision.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Names a decision at two or three stations, or describes what was done without identifying a choice.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Covers one station or none.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: States which process held dimensions best and worst from their own numbers, and gives a physical reason involving the tool, the beam, the material, or the setup.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: States the pattern from their own numbers and offers a reason that is correct but not tied to a specific process characteristic.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Reads the measurements out without saying what pattern they show, or names a pattern with no reason.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Does not refer to their own measurements.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Answers every question from what they did and measured, including at least one they had not prepared for.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Answers most questions from their own work, with one answer that restates a slide.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Answers mainly by reading slides aloud, or cannot answer more than one question.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Does not answer questions, or does not present.
